chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 397 – Li Huowang learns not to argue, Zhuge Yuan tells history
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang learns the fine art of agreeing without believing as Zhuge Yuan tries to start a 72-hour lecture on the Great Qi. Meanwhile, Lu Xiucai cheats at gambling, buys breakfast, and tastes his first real power.
og_title: Chen 397 of Dao Gui Yi Xian: Knowing Without Believing & a Wild Gambling Scene
og_description: Li Huowang taps out of a history lesson. Zhuge Yuan tries to lecture anyway. And Lu Xiucai discovers that rigging coin flips is way more fun than being told you’re useless.
twitter_title: Dao Twisted World Ch 397: One dude philosophizes, another one gambles—both are in over their heads.
twitter_description: Li Huowang accepts a lie for peace. Lu Xiucai cheats at gambling. This is the tonal whiplash we live for.

lore_anchors.definition: A person whose obsession is so powerful it becomes their entire identity, often tied to a vanished nation, person, or world. Unlike Heart-Elements, Heart-Pans cannot reshape reality spontaneously—but they carry their delusion like a full-time job.

Fictional dynasties from Zhuge Yuan’s background. The Great Qi is his “true” reality; the Great Liang is the “stolen beam swapped for a rotten timber” world that he believes is a forgery. Think of it as a xianxia version of a conspiracy theory about an alternate history matrix.
An oblique reference to a higher-tier metaphysical structure in the Dao-Twisted World’s cosmology, possibly relating to Siming or other celestial entities mentioned in passing.
A large, prosperous city in the Dao-Twisted World. Like all prosperous places, it has a thriving criminal underground—ditry gambling dens, loan sharks, and street thugs.

The owner of a gambling den in Yinling City. He splits the winnings with Lu Xiucai and advises him on how to manipulate gamblers: “give them a little taste, let them win three times out of ten, and they’ll keep coming back.”

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang just accept Zhuge Yuan’s story?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He doesn’t believe it, but he’s learned that arguing with someone who is equally trapped in their own reality is a waste of energy. He’s applying the survival lesson he learned in the hospital: “agree without committing.”

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Zhuge Yuan keep trying to lecture Li Huowang?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is a *shuoshuren* (storyteller) by nature. Historical exposition is his love language. Being cut off triggers a kind of intellectual withdrawal for him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Lu Xiucai going to become a major antagonist now?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Too early to call. This chapter gives him resources, street cred, and ego. That’s a dangerous combination in this world—especially when the Zuowandao are always looking for useful puppets.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does “stolen beam swapped for a rotten timber” mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: An ancient Chinese idiom for a deception where a good part is replaced with a bad one without the owner noticing. Zhuge Yuan uses it to describe how he thinks reality itself was swapped without anyone realizing it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the gambling scene matter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It acts as a tonal breather and a parallel arc. It shows that “power” in this world can be as small as a rigged coin flip. It also reminds us that Li Huowang isn’t the only one changing—the people he left behind are transforming too.
